description:
At HEAD 89db749f6 (2026-08-21) this is the ONLY matrix red without a live ticket, and it is no longer the failure the fz-go4.22 census recorded.

WAS: native.rs:3123 panic, 'backend value ValueId(N) must be runtime-materializable', on BOTH run and build.
IS:  ::interp and ::build are GREEN. ::run fails on WALL CLOCK ONLY -- 'fz2 exceeded 10s'. The panic is gone.

MEASURED directly, outside the harness:
  ./target/debug/fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz
  -> 11.77s user / 11.90s total, exit 0, output CORRECT (:ok / false / true / 1 / :first)

So this is not a timeout flake and not machine contention -- it is a reproducible ~19% overshoot of the budget on a fixture that produces the right answer. Per the standing convention (tiny fixtures must complete in ms-to-tenths; >1s is a correctness signal, not a perf one), 11.9s on a fixture this small means the compiler is doing a large amount of excess or repeated work on the JIT path specifically. The interp and build lanes clearing the same fixture bounds the problem to what run does differently.

DO NOT fix by raising the budget -- the budget is the detector.

FIRST STEP: --log-telemetry job trace, compare the job span census against the build lane (which compiles the same program without the overshoot); look for repeated productions / non-monotone re-settling in the fz-go4.18.28 transport-monolith family, which is the known shape for multi-second small fixtures.

REPRO: cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1 enum_predicate_search

comments.text:
FIXED at d828560c9 (PR #91, stacked on #90/fz-km1).

THE TICKET'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND SO WAS MINE, TWICE -- recording both so nobody re-derives them.

1. NOT JIT-lane excess work. All three lanes were slow; ::interp only 'passed' because its budget is 15s and it took 10.75s. Measured: run 12.20s, interp 10.75s, build 11.77s. The excess work was in the shared front half.

2. My first hypothesis (walk can stay inside one product kind, since every caller asks about same-kind from/target) was FALSE. transport_shape and callable_construction depend on each other, so the product kind graph has a real 2-cycle. The test I wrote to pin it failed -- which is the only reason it did not ship.

ROOT CAUSE. --log-telemetry put only 0.91s of 10.7s inside drive jobs. Attributing the gap before each product settle: callable_construction 2625 settles / 6704 ms. A sampling profile put 52% of the whole process in produce_generic_callable_owner -> ProductMemo::pending_dependency_reaches, mostly HashSet<ProductKey>::insert and SipHash.

Before waiting on a dependency a producer must know whether that dependency is waiting on it. That was answered by a fresh DFS over the ENTIRE product dependency graph, once per dependency per production, cloning and hashing a ProductKey per step: 3569 walks, 21.9M nodes visited, 15 cycles found. ~6136 nodes per walk to say 'no' 99.6% of the time.

THE FIX. Only an unsettled product can be waiting on anything; a settled one answers a read with the value it already holds, so no chain of waits runs through it. The walk now follows unsettled products only (in-flight or displaced) and holds references instead of cloning. 3585 walks, 9923 nodes, the SAME 15 cycles. Found by tracing what the 15 genuine cycles are made of: every node on every one was in-flight or in-progress, never settled.

Collapse: the gate and the strong component it gates were one question asked twice, differing only in a member filter the gate omitted. pending_dependency_reaches + dependency_reaches_with_current -> dependency_reaches; pending_transport_shape_group + pending_callable_construction_group -> pending_recursive_group; the member: fn(&ProductKey) -> bool parameter deleted.

Guarded by settled_products_depend_only_on_settled_products (product_drive_test.rs): drives a real reducer program and checks every memo edge, so the pruning is lossless and not merely safe. It also asserts both recursive kinds self-loop in that drive so it cannot pass vacuously.

RESULT: run 12.20 -> 3.88s, interp 10.75 -> 2.55s, build 11.77 -> 3.61s.

GATES: lib 1442/0; matrix 410 passed / 0 FAILED single-threaded -- the WHOLE matrix is green, this also cleared both enum_take_drop_split lanes (fz-f98.14's matrix reds) which were failing the same way; clippy --workspace --all-targets 0 warnings; fmt clean.

BUDGET: not raised. Lowered 10s/15s -> 6s/6s, just above measured, per 'the budget is the detector'.

NOT FIXED, ticketed: the fixture is still ~3s (2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables -- population or churn is unestablished) -> fz-xat. Other fixtures now carry timeout overrides far above their real cost, and enum_tier0 cites fz-g58.52 which does not exist -> fz-1iw.

title: enum_predicate_search::run exceeds the 10s fixture budget (11.9s) with correct output -- JIT-lane excess work
